investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent scheduling on the other 4 nodes. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck unscheduled until the resource is replenished or capacity is expanded. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the pod never starts, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885, createAgent call) never receives a VM ID or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only the 2 kata-capable nodes, so even if other nodes had spare CPU/memory, they cannot accept the pod. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, this could explain a new failure pattern.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, which may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads. A surge in remote agent demand could exhaust the pool.

Lower probability — eval probe concurrency: if multiple eval runs (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) submit pods simultaneously, they compete for the same limited VM slots, accelerating exhaustion within a single eval cycle.

If kubectl or equivalent tooling shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, quota, or admission webhook rejection).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent scheduling on the other 4 nodes. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck unscheduled until the resource is replenished or capacity is expanded. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the pod never starts, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885, createAgent call) never receives a VM ID or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 125s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=149794, endedAt=2026-06-20T22:32:04.885Z — confirms the condition persisted across a second independent probe attempt.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=151417, endedAt=2026-06-20T22:34:36.302Z — confirms the condition persisted across a third independent probe attempt spanning ~7 minutes total.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the agent pod never reaching a running state.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no partial progress was recorded, confirming the failure occurred before any agent lifecycle step completed.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; a pod scheduling failure at the infrastructure layer would prevent this call from returning any VM identity or state.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be satisfied if the pod is never scheduled.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=128885 (~128s), which exceeds the pod-stuck threshold of 125s named in the scheduler message, confirming the eval timed out waiting for pod readiness.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only the 2 kata-capable nodes, so even if other nodes had spare CPU/memory, they cannot accept the pod. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, this could explain a new failure pattern.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, which may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads. A surge in remote agent demand could exhaust the pool.

Lower probability — eval probe concurrency: if multiple eval runs (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) submit pods simultaneously, they compete for the same limited VM slots, accelerating exhaustion within a single eval cycle.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true with a valid remoteState, the exhaustion was transient and has since resolved — disproving a persistent capacity shortage.

If kubectl or equivalent tooling shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, quota, or admission webhook rejection).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and consequently zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected against the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry that resource. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With no schedulable node available and no preemption victims eligible, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~125–151 s), preventing the eval runner from ever reaching the agent-creation, state-polling, or runtime-chat steps. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 146s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical Unschedulable scheduler message, latencyMs=128885, endedAt=2026-06-20T22:29:35.091Z — the create check failed first with the same root cause.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable scheduler message, latencyMs=149794, endedAt=2026-06-20T22:32:04.885Z — sameMessage=true confirms the same scheduling block.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151417 — the eval waited the full scheduler timeout before failing, consistent with a pod stuck in Pending rather than an API error.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence fields were collected, confirming the agent pod never started and the runner never reached the runtime chat step.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting at createAgent before any evidence could be gathered.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId — if the pod never schedules, this call blocks and eventually surfaces the scheduler error as the check message.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the observed latencyMs=151417 is well under the outage threshold, so the feature-level outage gate has not been crossed by this check alone.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing peer-pods, leaving no capacity for new agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are even candidates for remote-agent pods. If those 2 nodes lose capacity, the entire remote-agent pool is blocked. A recent change to node labels or the pod spec's affinity rules could have reduced the eligible node pool.

TERTIARY — Leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user sessions may have left VMs running that were not cleaned up, consuming the finite VM resource budget on the 2 eligible nodes.

QUATERNARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for concurrent eval runs plus live user workloads, causing contention during the eval window.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Expect the same Unschedulable message if the VM capacity is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents checks together to confirm the shared scheduling failure
reproductionSteps.details: All three should reproduce the same Unschedulable scheduler message if the root cause is cluster-level VM exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the two eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl to describe the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and compare allocatable vs. requested quantities to confirm exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.label: List all running peer-pod VMs to identify leaked or zombie instances
reproductionSteps.details: Query the cluster for pods using the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource that are in Running or Pending state to determine whether prior eval runs or user sessions left VMs unreleased.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes peer-pod VM scheduling layer (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message directly names kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 nodes eligible for remote-agent pods. All three remote-agent checks are blocked at this layer (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents eval feature — checks: remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature failed with the same infrastructure scheduling error. remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false (source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189).

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent remote branch
affectedAreas.reason: The runner calls createAgent with type 'remote' at line 1918; this is the call that blocks waiting for the pod to schedule and ultimately surfaces the Unschedulable error (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918).

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: All 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) and the message assertion ('hello from aura') are unmet because the agent never started (expected-output.missing-required-evidence, source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270).

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the two eligible nodes to confirm exhaustion and determine how many slots are occupied vs. available.
Audit running peer-pod VMs for leaked or zombie instances from prior eval runs or user sessions; terminate any that are no longer needed to free VM slots.

Investigate whether the node affinity/selector configuration intentionally restricts remote-agent pods to only 2 of 6 nodes, and whether expanding the eligible node pool (or adding kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to additional nodes) is feasible.

Review the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm that eval-created remote-agent VMs are reliably released after each probe run, preventing capacity leaks across successive eval executions.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check to the remote-agent eval probes that queries available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before attempting pod creation, so the check can emit a more actionable SKIP or WARN status with capacity details rather than timing out.

Monitor the remote-agents feature degraded/outage thresholds: degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 (infra/evals/status/features.json lines 187–188); with all three checks currently failing, the feature is at or near the outage threshold for required checks.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe to check if the condition persists
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is ongoing or was transient. A pass would collect all 5 required evidence fields and satisfy the expected-output contract (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Describe the two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes to read current allocatable vs. used VM capacity
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms or refutes the VM exhaustion hypothesis from failed-check.message.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl describe node on each of the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and inspect the Allocatable and Allocated resources sections.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods currently consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources to identify leaks
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether zombie or leaked peer-pod VMs from prior eval runs or user sessions are consuming the finite VM budget.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl get pods --all-namespaces with a field selector or resource filter to enumerate pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node affinity/selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec to understand why 4 of 6 nodes are excluded
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the 4-node exclusion is intentional (e.g., only kata-capable nodes are eligible) or a misconfiguration that has reduced the schedulable pool.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Retrieve the pod spec or the agent creation template used by createAgent in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs and review nodeAffinity and nodeSelector fields.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared scheduling failure
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Verifies that all three checks reproduce the same Unschedulable message, confirming the failure is at the shared infrastructure layer rather than isolated to the runtime probe.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) VM slots, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or API error would need to be investigated.

If the 4 non-matching nodes were found to have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but were excluded only due to a node affinity/selector mismatch, the primary cause would shift from VM exhaustion to affinity misconfiguration.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and collects all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

If the sibling checks remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass on a subsequent run while remote-agent-runtime still fails, the failure would be isolated to the runtime probe rather than a shared scheduling constraint.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined on any node in the cluster, the failure would indicate a missing node configuration rather than exhaustion of an existing resource.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-vm-capacity) that queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used count on eligible nodes and warns before exhaustion reaches 100%, enabling proactive alerting before pod scheduling fails.

Add a remote-agent-vm-leak-detection check that counts peer-pod VMs older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) and fails if leaked VMs are detected, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust capacity.

Add a remote-agent-node-affinity check that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector rules, alerting if the eligible node pool shrinks below a minimum threshold.
Extend the existing remote-agent-create check to record the pod scheduling latency as an evidence field, enabling trend analysis to detect gradual capacity degradation before hard failures occur.
